name: detail_enlarges
why: ENTRY GT4, the other half. The section shows what is inside; the detail shows what is too small to be read at the scale of the drawing — a groove, a chamfer, a fillet with its dimension. Without it, on a workshop drawing those things are dimensioned by eye.
_why_the_hatch_is_not_checked: On the section the hatching says that the cut met material, and it is the check that counts. A detail cuts NOTHING: it shows the same geometry enlarged, and `GetFaceHatchCount` on the detail answers **0** (measured on 23/9/2026). Copying the check of the section would have produced an operation that always refuses — that is the defect the section had at first use, repeated by analogy.
defect_caught: A circle that stays hand-drawn next to an extra view that is not tied to it. `views_after` goes up in both cases. The proof that the circle BECAME a detail is that the starting view has one more detail circumference: from zero to one. The count is read from the RETURN VALUE of `GetDetailCircleCount2`, not from its `out` — the out goes from 1 to 35 for a single circumference, and whoever read it as a count would say the view already had one before having any.

expect.why: if the part is not the right one, neither is the drawing
a drawing is made on a saved part
from here on the active document is another one
without a model view there is nothing to detail

steps._why_x_mm_55: At the centre of the front view (120 x 20 mm at scale 1) a circle of radius 8 mm stays inside the face and the detail shows no edge: measured on 27/10/2026 (report 8cd843 N47, scenario t40), 0 visible edges at the centre, 1 with x_mm 55, where the circle takes the right end of the plate. Since library 0.174.4 an empty detail is refused (limit_detail_on_empty_space), so this case encloses an edge.

expect.why: the starting view had none: it is the term of comparison, and without it «there is one now» would not say that it was born now

expect._and_this_is_the_line_that_counts: **IT IS THE ONLY THING THAT TELLS A DETAIL FROM A HAND-DRAWN CIRCLE.** `views_after` goes up anyway: an extra view on the sheet does not say that it is tied to that circle. The detail circumference on the STARTING view says it.
expect.why: from zero to one, on the starting view
the type of the view born (swDrawingDetailView), not the fact that the count went up

the three model views, without the SHEET that the SOLIDWORKS list gives as its first «view»: counted as «inspect_part» and «model_view» count them (report 8cd843 N42, round 11: 5 here and 4 there on the same drawing, until library 0.174.1)
one more: the check that the API did not just answer an object
the blindness that counts: a circle moved by ten millimetres enlarges another edge, and it is just as valid
the right end of the plate, and nothing else: the circle landed where it was asked (report 8cd843 N47: with sheet coordinates in the sketch of the view the details were empty)
